entities.title: Result envelope of the JSON layer
entities.summary: Every JSON-layer function returns a Result, the utv-result/1.0 envelope, and never raises for a semantic outcome.
consumers: Application developers who use the JSON layer (utv.parse_iso, utv.add, utv.resolve, …)
The typed layer, through outcome_of and Outcome.to_result
tests/test_everyday_fixtures.py and tests/test_text_form.py, which compare results with the shared fixtures
guarantees: Result.to_dict() writes schema utv-result/1.0, operation, status, manifest, assumptions, loss and diagnostics, and candidates only when there are any.
operation carries the everyday name (parseIso, add, resolve, parseText, …), validate for the 0.1 checks and convert for utv.native.
unique has exactly one candidate (Result.value), multiple has all of them in ascending order, and every other status has none.

A semantic outcome is a status, never an exception. Wrong Python types raise TypeError; ZoneRules.parse and load_rules raise ValueError for a malformed bundle, while a malformed bundle passed to resolve or to_zone is invalid (malformed-value).
resolve and to_zone list the rule set they used in manifest.dependencies; resolve reports its loss as information-losing (zone, zoneIntent).

Diagnostics are {code, severity, path, message}. Codes follow docs/library-api.md §5, except that validate_structural and validate_gregorian_date still report their 0.1 codes (duplicate-key, unknown-kind, unknown-property, unsupported-kind, …).
The utv.native adapters put datetime objects in candidates instead of JSON, so to_dict() of their results is not JSON.
Outcome.to_result() returns the Result an outcome came from. outcome_of maps statuses that have no typed case (symbolic, resource-limit and the rest) to Unsupported.
entities.compatibility: Part of the package's 0.x API (implementations/python/.dev/contracts.json, utv-package). 0.3.0 renamed the JSON layer's diagnostic codes to the shared table and kept its functions and statuses (CHANGELOG.md).
